title: GET /books/{id} always returns 404, even for existing books
evidence: book_service.c:34 — the GET-by-id handler calls books_json(st,&b,0), whose while(sqlite3_step(st)==SQLITE_ROW) loop consumes every matching row and leaves the statement at SQLITE_DONE. It then computes `int found=sqlite3_data_count(st)>0`, but sqlite3_data_count() returns 0 after SQLITE_DONE (verified empirically: row stepped=1, data_count after loop=0), so `found` is always 0 and the handler returns error(c,404,"book not found") for every id, including ones that exist. The 404-when-absent case is correct by accident; the fetch-one-book path never succeeds.
suggestion: Capture the step result before/inside books_json (e.g. have books_json report whether it emitted a row, or check sqlite3_data_count immediately after a single sqlite3_step before consuming), then branch on that instead of calling data_count() after the statement has run to completion.

title: Unit tests never exercise the HTTP handler, so the R4 regression passes undetected
evidence: test_api.c:25-41 — test_sqlite_crud_and_author_filter drives execute_book()/sqlite3 directly and never calls handler(); the three tests cover json escaping, field parsing, and raw SQLite CRUD only. No test issues a GET /books/{id}, so test_coverage=1.0 does not validate the broken get-by-id route.
suggestion: Add at least one test that invokes the route logic (or a live-server integration test) for GET /books/{id} on an existing id, asserting HTTP 200 and the returned book body.
